summary: PDL on norm_gather -> rega w13 -> rega w2 is a sound, bit-identical, low-risk change with no prior in prefill. The stated mechanism overclaims, though: griddepcontrol.wait cannot hide the ±1-item tail. Only launch latency and the prologue overlap (barrier init, table decode, first weight stages), which realistically saves about 4-12 µs per shape, mostly at turn_1. Read the result from the per-class gate medians, not the headline or the per-kernel profile rows.
justification: Mechanism: plausible but smaller than claimed. rega_kernel is __launch_bounds__(THREADS,1) with near-full smem, so one CTA fits per SM. Early-launched w2 CTAs can only become resident on SMs where a w13 CTA has already exited, and they block at pdl_wait before any activation TMA or MMA. So w13's ±1-item tail is not recovered. What overlaps is (a) the graph kernel-to-kernel launch gap, about 1-3 µs per boundary, and (b) the prologue (mbar init, s_first/chunk table decode over nb blocks, tensormap prefetch, the first STAGES weight bulk copies, which are cold-L2 HBM latency because the judge flushes L2). That is about 2-6 µs per boundary times two boundaries, about 4-12 µs per shape. At turn_1 that is 0.5-1.5% of 756.7/1150.3 µs (the hypothesis says 10-25 µs, 2-3%). At turn_4 it is under 0.5%, and first_turn is flat. Expected directions are consistent with TASK weights; only the magnitude is optimistic. Correctness argument checks out against the code. sorted_ids, block_experts and n_padded come from align, which precedes the normally-launched gather, so they are complete before w13 can start. Weights and gs are static. The err magic and atomic writes before the wait are harmless. Every read of xs/hs and write of out/y sits behind pdl_wait, which also covers allocator-aliasing WAR hazards inside the captured graph. No deadlock: the rega grid is persistent and all CTAs are co-resident, so the explicit trigger fires only after every w13 CTA has issued or exited. Prior: 'none' is correct for prefill (grep finds no PDL in done/ or running/; DIAGNOSIS says griddepcontrol appears 0 times). The cited moe precedent (LESSONS 188, combo-toprow on PDL master) and attention combo-b1 (LESSONS 191) are real. It is not on any Do-not-try list. WEAKEST LINK: the gate. ON at <= 0.99x of the whole _experts_rega call (align + gather + w13 + w2 + post-norm) needs about 4.5-5 µs saved at turn_1, about 11 µs at turn_4 and about 55 µs at first_turn. turn_4 and first_turn will almost certainly gate OFF, so 'all three classes' is moot. turn_1 sits right at the threshold, which is exactly the single-round marginal-selector misroute the new LESSONS line warns about. Because the output is bit-identical and the change cannot plausibly cost much, a better gate is 'not slower' (ratio <= 1.00-1.01 over two interleaved cold-L2 rounds with an IQR bound), or an absolute-µs criterion. That keeps the small win on every class instead of a coin flip at 0.99.
confounders: combo-a-master-normgather-naive-stack (landed): the w13 primary is the Triton _norm_gather_kernel with a persistent grid of SMs x resident x NG_MULTS (1 or 2), chosen per class. With an implicit trigger at its exit, w13 overlap with the gather's tail depends on that grid choice. In classes where the gather is OFF, the primary is ext.rega_gather (one CTA per slot, a very different tail). Per-class savings at the gather->w13 boundary differ by which gather won, so this is not a confound of the sign, only of the magnitude.

w2-nonlocal-zero-store-off-first-turn (in stack-tonight-five-prefill, landed): when state['zero_nonlocal_w2'] is True, _experts_rega issues torch.zeros(y), a memset/fill node, between w13 and w2. w2's programmatic edge would then be against that node, not w13 (an invalid or ignored primary under capture). On the live rega path it is False (the ft class refuses otherwise), but the build must force pdl=0 for w2 whenever zero_nonlocal_w2 is True.

experts-turn-rega-s4-port-t4096 / experts-turn-rega-s4-first-turn-n128 (landed engine): the prologue PDL hides is this kernel's table decode. It is cheap in the small class (s_be in smem, about 50-100 blocks at T=753) and heavier in the BIG class (block_experts read through __ldg over thousands of blocks), so the overlap is per class. That is a property of the engine, not an interaction that could flip the sign.

combo-b-normgather-two-cta-low-regate (best's job; low variant gated OFF): if the low-class V64/V32 variant were ON, w13/w2 would run through state['rega_lo_ext'].rega_gemm_lo, which this change does not touch. Today variant=0, so the change does apply at turn_1. If a later restack turns V64 ON, PDL silently drops out of the low class.
interference: No companion is warranted. The change is bit-identical and self-gated. The prepare gate already times pdl=1 against pdl=0 in-process, interleaved under cold-L2 graph replay, and prints both medians per class, so that log line is the A/B. No landed hypothesis needs reverting to read it: the only real coupling (the zero_nonlocal_w2 memset node) is a correctness guard to build in, not something to measure. A control separating 'launch attribute only' from 'pre-wait prologue + weight prefetch' would split 4-12 µs into two pieces under okc noise and could not be read. Two reading rules make the single run interpretable. (1) Do NOT read the per-kernel profile rows: with PDL, rega_kernel<false,*> (and <true,*>, behind the gather) start earlier and spin in griddepcontrol.wait, so their reported durations GROW even when the shape gets faster. Read whole-shape µs and the gate medians. (2) The headline gain (about 0.3-0.8%) is below the 1.24% margin by the hypothesis's own admission, so score the run on the turn_1 gate ratio and the turn_1 shape rows, and carry it as a stack component (with mc2 / full-slab low) rather than judging it as a standalone submit.
rules_flags: No rules problem found. PDL is a launch attribute plus griddepcontrol; it keeps the graph-capturable, no-host-sync, no-input-branching contract, and the per-class pdl flag is a prepare-time plain int keyed on shape class. No precision change and no caching of input-derived data. The moe and attention PDL chains already ran on the judge.

Correctness hazard, not a rule: any xs/hs read or out/y write before griddepcontrol.wait is a silent race. The exact-compare must run under graph replay with pdl=1 (as the hypothesis says), over several routings including the 1.86x skew guard and one-expert/local-saturated cases, because a race may only show with short tails.
Guard needed: pdl must be 0 for w2 whenever state['zero_nonlocal_w2'] is True (a torch.zeros node sits between w13 and w2), and must be 0 on the rega_gemm_lo path unless that path is ported too.

Prepare budget: prepare already uses about 140 s of 300 s. Three more per-class cold-L2 interleaved gates plus graph-replay exact-compares must fit, and must not push ft setup past REGA_FT_START_DEADLINE_S (which would silently turn the ft class OFF and look like a large regression).
open_questions: Gate threshold: should the ON criterion be 'not slower' (<= 1.00-1.01, two interleaved rounds, IQR bound), given the output is bit-identical and the expected saving (about 1% at turn_1, under 0.5% elsewhere) is at or below the proposed 0.99x? As written, turn_4 and ft will almost surely gate OFF, and turn_1 is a marginal single-threshold selector (the 2026-10-25 LESSONS misroute pattern).

Producer restructure: issuing the first STAGES weight bulk_g2s before pdl_wait and that stage's activation tma_2d after it needs the expect_tx (WST + slab bytes) armed once per stage, before the weight copy, with the activation TMA completing the same transaction. Confirm the builder does not double-arm or under-count the full barrier.

Does the Triton _norm_gather_kernel launch interact with the programmatic attribute on w13 under torch graph capture (the primary is a Triton launch, not cudaLaunchKernelEx)? The moe precedent chained two CUDA-extension kernels, not Triton -> CUDA. Check that capture records a programmatic edge and not a full edge (a full edge would make the gather->w13 half a silent no-op).

Stacking with the queued mc2 / cluster line (experts-rega-mc2-*, rega_mc_kernel): the PDL attribute and the pdl_wait/pdl_launch placement have to be re-ported into the cluster kernel's cudaLaunchKernelEx (the cluster-dim attribute plus the programmatic attribute). Plan that port so a later mc2 win does not silently drop the PDL saving.
